requirements: The core contributions of Scepsy — an agentic serving system that uses Aggregate LLM Pipelines to jointly optimize GPU allocations for multi-LLM agentic workflows — have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware cluster, GPU interconnect topology, and software stack required to run Scepsy and its baselines have been set up.

The inter-machine and intra-machine GPU interconnect topology matches the paper: machines connected via 100 Gbps InfiniBand, and GPUs within a node connected as two NVLink pairs using 3rd-generation NVLink.
Inter-node networking is configured with 100 Gbps InfiniBand connectivity between the 4 machines, and this link is exposed to the cluster orchestrator for cross-node communication.

verification.spec: Run `ibstat` or `ip -s link show` on each node to verify a 100 Gbps InfiniBand interface is up and connected between nodes. Additionally verify the network is exposed to Kubernetes (e.g., check for a multus/RDMA network resource attachment definition).

sub_tasks.requirements: Intra-node GPU interconnect is set up so that the 4 GPUs on each node form two NVLink-connected pairs (3rd-generation NVLink), and NVLink domain membership is discoverable via nvidia-smi topo (or an equivalent query) for use by Scepsy's topology-aware placement.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi topo -m` on each node and verify that the 4 GPUs form two NVLink-connected pairs (i.e., the topology matrix shows NV* connectivity between exactly two pairs of GPUs, e.g., GPU0-GPU1 and GPU2-GPU3, with PCIe elsewhere). Confirm the output is machine-readable so Scepsy can extract NVLink domains.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented (or configuration provided) that enumerates NVLink domains per node and exposes them to Scepsy's placement algorithm, consistent with the 3rd-generation NVLink pair topology on the A6000 nodes.

verification.spec: Invoke Scepsy's node/topology enumeration routine on a node with A6000 GPUs. Verify that (1) NVLink domains are enumerated (e.g., pairs of GPUs connected via 3rd-gen NVLink), (2) each domain reports the participating GPU indices, and (3) the placement algorithm receives this list and can query it. Cross-check the enumerated domains against `nvidia-smi topo -m` output.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Kubernetes-based cluster orchestration stack used by Scepsy is installed and configured according to the paper.
MicroK8s v1.32 is installed on all 4 nodes and joined into a single Kubernetes cluster used by Scepsy for deployment.

verification.spec: Run `microk8s version` (or `kubectl version`) on the control node and confirm the server version reports v1.32.x. Then run `kubectl get nodes` and verify 4 Ready nodes are joined into the cluster.

sub_tasks.requirements: The NVIDIA Kubernetes device plugin has been installed and extended to support Scepsy's intra-node fractional GPU placement (i.e., locking specific GPUs/fractions to specific pods rather than random assignment).

verification.spec: Deploy two test pods that request specific GPU IDs / fractions via the extended device plugin's annotations or resource requests. Confirm via `nvidia-smi` inside each pod that the pod sees exactly the requested GPU indices/fractions (not a random assignment). Also verify the DaemonSet for the device plugin exists in `kube-system` and its image differs from the stock nvidia-device-plugin (e.g., contains 'scepsy' in the image tag).

sub_tasks.requirements: NVIDIA MPS is enabled on each GPU node and configured with static per-client limits on streaming multiprocessors (SMs) and GPU memory, so that GPU fractions co-located on the same GPU are isolated as described in Section 6.

verification.spec: On each GPU node, verify the MPS control daemon is running (`pgrep nvidia-cuda-mps-control`), and that pods spec has env vars CUDA_MPS_ACTIVE_THREAD_PERCENTAGE and CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT set (static per-client SM and memory limits). Deploy a test pod pair and confirm resource caps are enforced (attempting to exceed the mem limit fails with OOM).

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM serving engines and request routers used by Scepsy are installed at the versions specified in Section 7.1.
vLLM v0.17 is installed and used as the LLM serving engine for Scepsy and the Kubernetes/Aegaeon experiments, with one vLLM engine per replica as described in Section 6.

verification.spec: Run `pip show vllm` (or inspect the container image used by Scepsy replicas) and confirm the vLLM version is 0.17.x. Also verify the Scepsy deployment templates reference this vLLM version and that one vLLM engine is instantiated per replica pod.

sub_tasks.requirements: SGLang Model Gateway v0.3 (the SGLang router) is installed and configured as the per-workflow request router providing load- and KV-cache-aware routing.

verification.spec: Inspect the Kubernetes deployment for the SGLang Model Gateway (or the process launched by Scepsy) and verify the image/binary reports version 0.3.x. Send a test request and confirm the response headers or logs identify it as SGLang router with KV-cache-aware routing enabled.

sub_tasks.requirements: A second, separate environment with vLLM v0.2 is available for the Ayo baseline experiments, isolated from the main vLLM v0.17 installation so both can be used in the evaluation.

verification.spec: Confirm a separate Python virtualenv/conda env or container image exists with vLLM v0.2.x installed (via `pip show vllm` inside that env), and that the Ayo baseline scripts point to this env rather than the v0.17 env. Verify both vLLM versions can be launched independently without conflicts.

sub_tasks.requirements: GPU drivers, CUDA runtime, and Python dependencies needed by vLLM, SGLang, and Scepsy (25K LoC Python) are installed and validated.
NVIDIA GPU drivers and a CUDA toolkit version compatible with vLLM v0.17, vLLM v0.2, and the RTX A6000 GPUs are installed on all nodes, and nvidia-smi reports all 4 GPUs per node as healthy.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi` and confirm all GPUs on each node are healthy and detected. Verify installed CUDA/driver versions are compatible with vLLM v0.17 and vLLM v0.2 by installing both versions in isolated environments and running `python -c 'import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)'` successfully for each.

sub_tasks.requirements: A Python environment (matching Scepsy's requirements) is set up with all Scepsy dependencies installed, and running `python -c 'import scepsy'` (or the equivalent entrypoint) succeeds without errors.

verification.spec: Create a Python environment matching Scepsy's requirements file and run `python -c 'import scepsy'` (or the equivalent module entrypoint documented in the repo). Verify the command returns exit code 0 without ImportError.

sub_tasks.requirements: A smoke-test script confirms end-to-end infrastructure health by deploying a single vLLM replica through MicroK8s with the extended NVIDIA device plugin, requesting a fractional GPU with MPS-enforced SM/memory limits, and returning a successful completion.

verification.spec: Run the Scepsy smoke-test: (1) start MicroK8s with the extended NVIDIA device plugin enabled; (2) deploy a single vLLM replica requesting a fractional GPU (e.g., 0.5 GPU) via the plugin, with MPS enforcing SM/memory limits; (3) send a completion request to the deployed replica; (4) assert a successful HTTP 200 response with a non-empty completion. Verify MPS is active via `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` and that SM/memory limits are applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: The RAG+reranker and beam search agentic workflows, along with their LLMs (e5-base-v2, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.1-8B-PRM, Llama-2-7b, math-shepherd), have been prepared.
The RAG+reranker agentic workflow has been implemented and its associated models and datasets acquired.

Code has been implemented to define the RAG+reranker workflow as an agentic pipeline that queries a retriever/embedding LLM, applies a reranker, and finally generates an answer via a generator LLM, based on the FlashRAG reference implementation.

verification.spec: Import the RAG+reranker workflow module and instantiate the pipeline. Verify that (1) the workflow object exposes three distinct stages in order: an embedding/retriever LLM call, a reranker call, and a generator LLM call; (2) calling the workflow with a sample query string produces a generated answer string, and intermediate hooks/traces show the retriever was called before the reranker, and the reranker before the generator; (3) the retriever returns a ranked list of documents, the reranker reorders/filters this list, and the generator receives the reranked context. Use mocked LLM endpoints returning canned responses to avoid GPU dependency.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to download and load the e5-base-v2 embedding model as the retriever LLM component of the RAG+reranker workflow.

verification.spec: Verify that the RAG+reranker workflow loads intfloat/e5-base-v2 as the retriever/embedding LLM. Check that the HuggingFace model files are downloaded and that the embedding LLM component in the workflow uses this model id. Run a small embedding request and confirm output dimensionality matches e5-base-v2 (768-dim).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to download and load Llama-3-8B as the generator LLM in the RAG+reranker workflow (and Llama-2-7b when running against the older vLLM v0.2 baseline).

verification.spec: Verify the RAG+reranker workflow config loads meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B as the generator LLM. Confirm the model can be loaded via vLLM v0.17 and that the workflow-config for the vLLM v0.2 baseline path uses meta-llama/Llama-2-7b instead. Perform a single generation request through the generator and assert non-empty output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load a reranker component (e.g., a sequence-to-sequence document ranker following Nogueira et al.) that scores retrieved documents before generation.

verification.spec: Load the reranker component used in the RAG+reranker workflow (a document-ranker following Nogueira et al.). Feed it a query and a list of candidate documents; verify it returns a scored/ranked list where each document has a numeric score and the ordering changes based on relevance. Confirm the component is invoked between retrieval and generation in the workflow.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to prepare a workload of representative RAG+reranker requests (queries and associated corpora) suitable for driving arrival-rate sweeps used in the end-to-end and ablation experiments.

verification.spec: Verify a workload driver exists that generates RAG+reranker requests (queries + corpora) and supports arrival-rate sweeps (e.g., a Poisson-driven request generator with configurable req/s). Run it briefly at a low rate and confirm it emits requests at approximately the specified rate.

sub_tasks.requirements: The RAG+reranker workflow, when executed end-to-end, produces LLM invocations for the embedding model, the reranker, and the generator per request in the expected serial ordering.

verification.spec: Send a single request through the RAG+reranker workflow and capture the trace via the HTTP proxy. Assert that the trace contains, in serial order: (1) at least one embedding/retriever invocation, (2) at least one reranker invocation, and (3) one generator invocation, with timestamps confirming serial ordering.

sub_tasks.requirements: The beam search agentic workflow has been implemented and its associated generator and verifier LLMs acquired.

Code has been implemented to define the beam search workflow with inference-time scaling that iteratively expands candidate reasoning steps with a generator LLM, scores them with a verifier LLM, and retains top-k beams until termination, based on HuggingFace's search-and-learn reference.

verification.spec: Instantiate the beam search workflow. Send a math problem and verify: (1) it iteratively expands candidate reasoning steps via the generator LLM, (2) scores each candidate with the verifier LLM, (3) retains top-k beams for the next iteration, and (4) terminates on a done condition, producing a final answer. Confirm the implementation follows HuggingFace's search-and-learn reference structure.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to download and load Llama-3.2-1B as the generator LLM in beam search (and Llama-2-7b when running against the older vLLM v0.2 baseline).

verification.spec: Verify the beam search workflow config loads meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B as the generator LLM (and the vLLM v0.2 baseline path uses meta-llama/Llama-2-7b). Load the model via vLLM and execute a single generation call to confirm success.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to download and load Llama-3.1-8B-PRM as the process-reward-model verifier LLM in beam search (and math-shepherd when running against the older vLLM v0.2 baseline).

verification.spec: Verify the beam search workflow config loads RLHFlow/Llama3.1-8B-PRM-Mistral-Data (or the equivalent Llama-3.1-8B-PRM checkpoint referenced by the paper) as the verifier LLM, and that the vLLM v0.2 baseline path uses the math-shepherd model. Load the verifier and score a sample generation to confirm it produces a numeric process-reward score.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to prepare a workload of math-reasoning problems used to drive beam search requests at varying arrival rates for profiling and evaluation.

verification.spec: Verify a workload driver exists that emits beam search requests based on math-reasoning problems (e.g., MATH or GSM8K) at configurable arrival rates. Run it briefly and confirm it emits math problems as prompts at approximately the specified req/s.

sub_tasks.requirements: The beam search workflow, when executed, exhibits data-dependent branching and fan-out (parallel beam expansions) and can be traced to yield multiple generator/verifier LLM invocations per request in the expected iterative pattern.

verification.spec: Run the beam search workflow for a handful of requests and capture their traces. Assert: (1) each request contains multiple generator invocations (indicating iterative branching), (2) each request contains multiple verifier invocations, (3) some generator invocations occur concurrently in wallclock time (fan-out for parallel beam expansion), and (4) different requests exhibit different invocation counts (data-dependent branching).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload characterization statistics of the prepared workflows match those reported in the paper.
The number of generator LLM invocations per beam search request, measured over the prepared trace, spans approximately from 24 to 844 as reported in Section 2.1.

verification.spec: Run the beam search workflow trace collection over a representative set of requests (matching the paper's setup) and, for each workflow request, count the number of generator LLM invocations. Report the min and max across requests and confirm the maximum is close to 844 (and minimum near 24).

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end request latency of the beam search workflow, measured over the prepared trace, ranges approximately from 9 to 264 seconds as reported in Section 2.1.

verification.spec: Execute the beam search workflow over a batch of representative requests, record per-request end-to-end wall-clock latency, and report the min and max. Confirm the maximum is ~264 s (and min ~9 s).

sub_tasks.requirements: Distributions of relative (fraction-of-total) execution times per LLM for beam search are computed and are up to ~4x more stable (narrower) than the absolute distributions, matching the claim illustrated in Fig. 3b.

verification.spec: From the beam search execution traces, compute per-request absolute execution time per LLM and per-request relative fraction of total execution time per LLM. Compute the coefficient of variation (or interquartile range) for both distributions across the two LLMs (generator, verifier) and confirm the relative distributions are up to ~4x more stable (i.e., relative CV is ~1/4 of absolute CV) for at least one LLM.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Scepsy GPU scheduler enumerates fractional GPU allocations, packs fractions onto GPUs, resolves tensor parallelism and replica configurations, and applies latency-ratio pruning to find allocations that minimize latency subject to a target workflow arrival rate.

Step 1 of the scheduler enumerates candidate mappings from LLMs to GPU fractions, using latency-ratio-guided pruning, minimum/maximum per-LLM fraction bounds, and contiguity constraints to keep the search tractable.

Code has been implemented that computes per-LLM latency ratios from an Aggregate LLM Pipeline (each LLM's profiled per-request latency divided by the sum of latencies across all LLMs in the pipeline).

verification.spec: Construct an ALP with 3 LLMs having known per-request latencies (e.g., 3.5, 1.6, 3.6). Call the latency-ratio function and assert returned ratios equal each latency divided by the sum (matches Fig. 5 example: 0.40, 0.18, 0.41 approximately) within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: The enumerator orders LLMs by descending latency ratio and enforces that in any enumerated fractional allocation, an LLM with a higher latency ratio never receives fewer GPU fractions than an LLM with a lower latency ratio.

verification.spec: Invoke the enumerator with 3 LLMs whose latency ratios are (0.6, 0.3, 0.1). Collect all enumerated allocations and assert that in every enumerated allocation the GPU-fraction assigned to LLM_1 >= LLM_2 >= LLM_3. Also assert LLMs are indeed processed in descending latency-ratio order.

sub_tasks.requirements: The enumerator computes a per-LLM minimum GPU fraction sufficient to load model parameters plus initialize its KV cache, and uses this as a lower bound in enumeration.

verification.spec: Instantiate the enumerator with a mock LLM whose parameter size and KV cache reservation are known (e.g., 8GB weights + 2GB KV cache on a 48GB GPU). Assert the computed minimum GPU fraction is ceil((8+2)/48 * F)/F where F is fractions-per-GPU. Assert the enumerator never emits candidates below this fraction for the LLM.

sub_tasks.requirements: The upper bound on GPU fractions per LLM is derived by subtracting the sum of minimum GPU fractions of all lower-latency LLMs from the total GPU-fraction budget, and the enumerator restricts search to this range.

verification.spec: Set up an enumerator with 3 LLMs ordered by descending latency ratio with known minimum fractions m1, m2, m3 and total budget B. Enumerate candidates and assert the highest-latency LLM's allocated fraction never exceeds B - (m2 + m3), and analogously for the second LLM.

sub_tasks.requirements: The enumerator quantizes GPU allocations in increments of 1/F of a GPU (where F is the configured fractions-per-GPU granularity, e.g., 10 in the paper) and enumerates all compositions of the total fraction budget across LLMs at this granularity, subject to the ordering and bound constraints.

verification.spec: Configure the enumerator with F=10 fractions-per-GPU, 4 GPUs total (budget = 40 units), and 2 LLMs. Assert every emitted allocation's per-LLM fraction is an integer multiple of 1/10, sums to 4.0, and the enumeration count matches the expected number of ordered compositions subject to bounds.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler limits enumerated tensor parallel degrees to at most the high-bandwidth (NVLink) domain size and skips any candidate whose per-replica tensor parallel degree exceeds that limit.

verification.spec: Configure a cluster topology with NVLink domain size 2. Run the scheduler over a workload where TP=4 would otherwise be enumerated. Assert no candidate allocation with TP > 2 is emitted, and candidates with TP in {1, 2} are still enumerated.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 2 packs each LLM's aggregate GPU fraction onto physical GPUs contiguously so that highest-latency LLMs are least fragmented across GPUs.

Code has been implemented that, given a per-LLM total GPU-fraction value (e.g., 1.66 GPUs), packs it as consecutive whole-GPU fractions of size 1.0 followed by one partial-GPU fraction (e.g., 1.0 on GPU i and 0.66 on GPU i+1).

verification.spec: Call the packing function with fraction=1.66 starting at GPU index 0. Assert output is [(GPU 0, 1.0), (GPU 1, 0.66)]. Repeat with 2.5 and assert output is [(GPU 0, 1.0), (GPU 1, 1.0), (GPU 2, 0.5)].

sub_tasks.requirements: Packing processes LLMs in descending order of latency ratio so that higher-latency LLMs receive contiguous whole-GPU blocks before smaller LLMs are packed into remaining fractions.

verification.spec: Provide packing with 3 LLMs having latency ratios [0.6, 0.3, 0.1] and fractions [2.5, 1.2, 0.3]. Assert LLM 0 is packed into contiguous GPUs 0-2, LLM 1 next, LLM 2 last. Reverse the input order and assert output ordering by latency ratio is unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: Packing rejects any candidate in which an LLM's fractions would need to be split non-contiguously across GPUs (i.e., only contiguous per-LLM allocations are produced).

verification.spec: Set up a packing scenario where an LLM's fraction would need to split across GPUs 0 and 2 (skipping GPU 1 already occupied by another LLM). Assert the packer either rejects the candidate or reorders to keep the LLM contiguous. Iterate over all emitted packings and assert per-LLM GPU indices form a contiguous range.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 3 resolves feasible (tensor parallelism, replica count) combinations for each LLM given its packed GPU footprint, discarding infeasible or wasteful combinations.
Code has been implemented that enumerates candidate (TP, replicas) pairs for each LLM given its number of allocated (possibly fractional) GPUs.

verification.spec: Call the (TP, replicas) enumeration function for an LLM allocated 4 GPUs. Assert returned pairs include (1,4), (2,2), (4,1) but exclude (3,x) since 3 does not divide 4. For fractional 1.5 GPUs, assert TP=1 with sub-GPU-fraction is emitted and no TP>1 configurations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler discards (TP, replicas) combinations for which TP * replicas does not evenly divide the number of GPUs allocated to that LLM (avoiding under- or over-utilization as described in Section 5, step 3).

verification.spec: Call the parallelism-resolution routine for an LLM given 3 GPUs. Assert the returned (TP, replicas) combinations satisfy (TP * replicas) % 3 == 0 (e.g., includes (1,3), (3,1); excludes (2,1), (1,2), (2,2)). Repeat with 4 GPUs and check (1,1),(1,2),(1,4),(2,1),(2,2),(4,1) are candidates while (3,1),(1,3) are rejected.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler discards (TP, replicas) combinations where TP exceeds the NVLink high-bandwidth domain size, matching the tensor-parallel pruning rule described in Section 5.

verification.spec: Set the NVLink high-bandwidth domain size to 2 (matching A6000 pairs) in the scheduler configuration and call the parallelism-resolution routine with 8 GPUs allocated. Assert that no returned (TP, replicas) combination has TP>2 (e.g., (4,2) and (8,1) are pruned; (2,4) and (1,8) are kept).

sub_tasks.requirements: For sub-GPU allocations (LLMs assigned less than one full GPU), the scheduler forces TP=1 and replicas=1 and treats the LLM as sharing a GPU with other LLMs.

verification.spec: Invoke the parallelism enumerator with an LLM allocated 0.5 GPUs. Assert the only emitted configuration has TP=1 and replicas=1, and the placement flags this LLM as GPU-shared.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler queries the Aggregate LLM Pipeline predictor to score candidate allocations by predicted (throughput, latency) under a chosen latency percentile.

For each candidate allocation, the scheduler looks up the per-LLM workflow-level throughput-latency curve at the corresponding TP degree and target latency percentile P, evaluates L_wm at scaled arrival rate lambda_w * n_m / d_m, and combines them via equations (1) and (2) from Section 4.

verification.spec: Populate an ALP with synthetic profiles at TP=1,2 and percentile P50. For a candidate (d_m=2 replicas, TP=2), invoke the predictor with lambda_w=10. Assert it looks up the TP=2 curve at rate lambda_w * n_m / d_m and returns L_wm = L_m * n_m / p_m per eq. (1). Assert combined L_w equals sum over LLMs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Prediction lookups are implemented as O(1) profile-table lookups plus arithmetic, without invoking any additional LLM profiling at scheduling time.

verification.spec: Instrument the predictor code path to count profiling invocations (LLM launches or replays). Run 1000 predictor calls in a tight loop and assert zero profiling invocations occur. Time the calls and assert median call latency is under 1 ms.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler exposes hooks/CLI entry points for reproducing the search-time microbenchmark, sweeping (num LLMs, num GPUs, fractions per GPU) independently while holding the other two fixed.

verification.spec: Locate the scheduler microbenchmark CLI entry point. Invoke it with --sweep num_llms, --sweep num_gpus, and --sweep fractions_per_gpu independently. Assert each invocation exits 0 and produces output containing search-time measurements per swept value.

sub_tasks.requirements: The baseline systems Kubernetes HPA, Aegaeon (with 3P/1D, 2P/2D, 1P/3D configurations), and Ayo have been deployed for comparison against Scepsy.

Kubernetes HPA autoscaler baseline has been set up on MicroK8s v1.32 with vLLM v0.17 serving engines and SGLang Model Gateway v0.3 routing, matching the paper's software stack for the autoscaling comparison.

Code has been implemented to deploy each LLM in the RAG+reranker workflow (e5-base-v2 and Llama-3-8B) and the beam search workflow (Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.1-8B-PRM) as independently scalable Kubernetes Deployments backed by vLLM v0.17 engines behind an SGLang Model Gateway v0.3 router.

verification.spec: Apply the manifests for RAG+reranker (e5-base-v2, meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B) and beam search (meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B, RLHFlow/Llama3.1-8B-PRM-Mistral-Data) to the cluster. Assert each LLM runs as a separate Kubernetes Deployment, each pod runs vLLM v0.17, and an SGLang Model Gateway v0.3 router successfully proxies completion requests to each.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that configures Kubernetes HorizontalPodAutoscaler resources for each LLM deployment with resource-metric-based scaling policies (e.g., GPU utilization or KV cache usage) so that replicas scale up and down in response to load.

verification.spec: Inspect the K8s HPA baseline manifests: assert one HorizontalPodAutoscaler resource per LLM Deployment, with spec.metrics referencing a resource metric (e.g., GPU utilization via custom-metrics or KV-cache-usage). Apply and, under a load ramp, verify with `kubectl get hpa` that replica counts change (scale up and down) in response.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Kubernetes HPA baseline runs on the same 16-GPU cluster (4 nodes × 4 A6000 GPUs) as Scepsy, and supports being restricted to 4-GPU, 8-GPU, and 16-GPU subsets for the throughput-latency sweeps.

verification.spec: Bring up the K8s HPA baseline on the full 16-GPU cluster (4 nodes × 4 A6000). Verify a config flag or node-selector restricts the baseline to 4-GPU, 8-GPU, and 16-GPU subsets in three separate runs; check `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows pods only on the intended nodes for each.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that drives the Kubernetes HPA baseline with the same workflow client, arrival-rate sweeps (RAG+reranker: 1–28, 2–56, 4–112 req/s for 4/8/16 GPUs; beam search: matching sweeps) and measures achieved throughput and average end-to-end workflow latency for each rate.

verification.spec: Run the Scepsy client against the K8s HPA baseline using the arrival-rate sweeps in Section 7.2 (RAG+reranker at 1-28, 2-56, 4-112 req/s on 4/8/16 GPUs; beam search matching). For each rate, produce a log/CSV of achieved throughput and average end-to-end workflow latency, and verify the CSV contains one row per (workflow, GPU count, arrival rate) tuple.

sub_tasks.requirements: Aegaeon has been deployed as a multi-LLM multiplexing baseline with disaggregated prefill/decode instances and the three per-node P/D configurations (3P/1D, 2P/2D, 1P/3D) required by the paper.

The Aegaeon artifact (Zenodo record 16673199) has been obtained and built such that its prefill and decode serving instances, with token-level auto-scaling across models, execute on the evaluation cluster's A6000 GPUs.

verification.spec: Download the Aegaeon artifact from Zenodo record 16673199, build the container/binary, and launch its prefill and decode instances on an A6000 GPU. Send a test completion request to a prefill instance and verify it responds successfully, confirming the baseline is operational on the evaluation cluster.

sub_tasks.requirements: Aegaeon deployment configurations have been created for three per-node prefill/decode splits, 3P/1D, 2P/2D, and 1P/3D (four instances per node), and are launched on a single 4-GPU node for the 4-GPU experiments.

verification.spec: Inspect the Aegaeon deployment configs used in Section 7.2: verify three separate configurations named 3P/1D, 2P/2D, and 1P/3D exist, each launching four instances per node with the specified prefill:decode counts. Launch each on a 4-GPU node and confirm `docker ps` (or equivalent) shows the correct number of prefill and decode containers.

sub_tasks.requirements: For 8-GPU experiments Aegaeon is deployed across two nodes using the same per-node P/D configurations (6P/2D, 4P/4D, 2P/6D in aggregate), matching the configurations reported in the paper's 8-GPU figure.

verification.spec: Inspect the Aegaeon 8-GPU deployment configuration files/scripts and verify that they span two nodes with per-node prefill/decode splits of 3P/1D, 2P/2D, and 1P/3D (aggregate 6P/2D, 4P/4D, 2P/6D). Confirm by parsing config manifests or Kubernetes deployment yamls.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that non-LLM models used in the workflows (the RAG reranker and the e5-base-v2 embedding model) are served via Aegaeon's prefill instances, as stated in the paper.

verification.spec: Inspect the Aegaeon integration code and verify that RAG rerankers and the e5-base-v2 embedding model are routed to Aegaeon's prefill instance class (not decode). Check via config file/router code showing the mapping of these non-generative models to prefill workers.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Aegaeon baseline is driven by the same workflow-level clients as Scepsy for RAG+reranker and beam search, and per-configuration throughput and average latency are recorded across arrival-rate sweeps on 4 and 8 GPUs.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark harness against the Aegaeon baseline for RAG+reranker and beam search at 4 and 8 GPUs, verifying the same workflow client sweeps arrival rates and produces a machine-readable log with (throughput, avg_latency) for each configuration.
